events.title: The death of Thomas à Kempis
events.shortBlurb: The canon of the Devotio Moderna died at Mount St. Agnes, long held to be author of the Imitation of Christ…
body: Thomas Haemerken, Thomas of Kempen, was born about 1380 in that small Rhineland town, the son of a craftsman. Sent at thirteen to school at Deventer, he was formed by the Brethren of the Common Life, the followers of Geert Groote whose 'new devotion', the Devotio Moderna, taught a practical piety of humility, interior prayer, and the patient copying of good books.

In 1399 he entered the Augustinian canons of Mount St. Agnes near Zwolle, where his elder brother John was prior; he received the habit in 1406 and was ordained priest in 1413. For seventy-two years he served that house as novice master and twice as subprior, copying manuscripts, for he copied out the whole Bible four times, and writing small treatises of the spiritual life.

He died at Mount St. Agnes on 25 July 1471. By long tradition he is held to be the author of The Imitation of Christ, written in the years about 1418 to 1427; after the Sacred Scriptures no Christian book has been more translated or more read, and its quiet counsels of humility and detachment from the world have formed souls for five hundred years.
